bibl.title: Spatial responsiveness of monkey hippocampal neurons to various visual and auditory stimuli

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Of 1,047 neurons recorded, 106 (10.1%) responded to some stimuli from one or more directions.

span.label: spatial responsiveness of monkey hippocampal neurons
span.quote: To investigate involvement of the hippocampal formation in spatial information processing, activity of neurons in the hippocampal formation of the conscious monkey was recorded during presentation of various visual and auditory stimuli from several directions around the monkey.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Briefly, single-unit activity was recorded from the HF and PH.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: spatial information is converted from a primary retinotopic representation into egocentric or allocentric representations somewhere between the sensory association cortices and the hippocampal formation / parahippocampal cortices
span.quote: Therefore, some computation or conversion of information from the primary step of spatial representation (such as retinotopic space) to a more complicated spatial representation (such as egocentric or allocentric space) may be made between the sensory association cortices and the H F and PH, or within the H F and PH.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: prolonged attention directed to one region of space during training and recording recruits more neurons that encode stimulus relations in that region
span.quote: If learning or memory should be related to neuronal activity, it might be possible that the increased time of attention to that area caused the difference seen in the number of neurons, that is, more neurons represent relations to various combinations of stimuli that were seen in the right anterior.

span.label: Responses that changed independently of the apparatus movement resist interpretation.
span.note: what this limits: the subset of neurons whose responses did not track the apparatus: IT IS DIFFICULT TO INTERPRET RESPONSIVENESS OF NEURONS THAT CHANGE IRRESPECTIVE OF MOVEMENT OF THE APPARATUS
span.quote: It is difficult to interpret responsiveness of neurons that change irrespective of movement of the apparatus.

span.label: Alternative explanations, such as suppression by stimuli not visible in the usual position, cannot be ruled out for the neurons whose responsiveness was extinguished.
span.note: what this limits: the spatial interpretation of the responses: OTHER FACTORS MIGHT HAVE INFLUENCED THE RESPONSIVENESS, SUCH AS SUPPRESSION BY PARTICULAR STIMULI THAT COULD NOT BE SEEN IN THE USUAL POSITION
span.quote: However, other factors might have influenced the responsiveness, such as suppression by particular stimuli that could not be seen in the usual position.

span.label: The directional bias of visual versus auditory responsiveness is not fully explained and may be an artefact of the training and recording set-up.
span.note: what this limits: the visual-versus-auditory asymmetry: THE REASONS FOR THIS DISCRIMINATION ARE NOT ENTIRELY CLEAR, and the offered account is a plausibility argument about what is useful to the monkey
span.quote: The reasons for this discrimination are not entirely clear, but it seems reasonable that vision should depend on stimuli presented within the visual field, and audition might be more valuable to the monkey when stimuli cannot be seen.

span.label: Where the conversion from retinotopic to egocentric or allocentric representation occurs is not resolved by these data.
span.note: what this limits: any claim about where the coordinate conversion happens: FURTHER STUDIES ARE NECESSARY TO INVESTIGATE SUCH COMPUTATION OR CONVERSION
span.quote: Further studies are necessary to investigate such computation or conversion.

span.label: The largest of the three response groups is left unnamed and absent from the paper's key words.
span.note: what this limits: any use of the egocentric/allocentric dichotomy from this paper: of the 32 neurons tested by rotation, 11 followed the monkey and 9 remained fixed to the environment, while 12 - the largest group - were reversibly extinguished and received no label
span.quote: Thirty-two of 106 neurons were also tested by rotating the monkey. The directionally differentiating responsiveness of 1 1 neurons followed the monkey (egocentric neurons), that of 9 remained in place in the environment (allocentric neurons), and responses of 12 were reversibly extinguished when the monkey was rotated

span.label: The egocentric category is defined to include stimuli fixed to the restraining apparatus, not only to the body.
span.note: what this limits: any reading of these egocentric neurons as body-centred: the designation covers responses considered to represent relations to background stimuli on the monkey OR on the restraining device that rotated with it
span.quote: We designate these neurons as “egocentric,” because the directions of their responses followed the rotation of the monkey, and these responses were considered to represent relations between the test stimulus and background stimuli on the monkey or on the restraining device that rotated with the monkey

span.label: egocentric
span.quote: We designate these neurons as “egocentric,” because the directions of their responses followed the rotation of the monkey, and these responses were considered to represent relations between the test stimulus and background stimuli on the monkey or on the restraining device that rotated with the monkey

span.label: allocentric
span.quote: We designated these neurons as “allocentric,” because the directions of their responses did not follow the rotation of the monkey but remained constant relative to the environment

span.label: restraining device
span.quote: We designate these neurons as “egocentric,” because the directions of their responses followed the rotation of the monkey, and these responses were considered to represent relations between the test stimulus and background stimuli on the monkey or on the restraining device that rotated with the monkey

span.label: directionally differentiating responsiveness
span.quote: Thirty-two of 106 neurons were also tested by rotating the monkey. The directionally differentiating responsiveness of 1 1 neurons followed the monkey (egocentric neurons), that of 9 remained in place in the environment (allocentric neurons), and responses of 12 were reversibly extinguished when the monkey was rotated

span.label: reversibly extinguished
span.quote: Thirty-two of 106 neurons were also tested by rotating the monkey. The directionally differentiating responsiveness of 1 1 neurons followed the monkey (egocentric neurons), that of 9 remained in place in the environment (allocentric neurons), and responses of 12 were reversibly extinguished when the monkey was rotated

span.label: egocentric, here - A LABEL FROM ONE ROTATION, AND WIDER THAN BODY-CENTRED: neurons are so designated because their response directions followed the rotation of the monkey, and the relations meant are to background stimuli on the monkey OR ON THE RESTRAINING DEVICE that rotated with it, so apparatus-fixed and body-fixed responses fall under one name
span.quote: We designate these neurons as “egocentric,” because the directions of their responses followed the rotation of the monkey, and these responses were considered to represent relations between the test stimulus and background stimuli on the monkey or on the restraining device that rotated with the monkey

span.label: allocentric, here - THE COMPLEMENT OF THE SAME OPERATION: neurons whose response directions did not follow the rotation but remained constant relative to the environment; both categories are produced by a single manipulation, and 'were considered to represent' marks where the operation ends and the interpretation begins
span.quote: We designated these neurons as “allocentric,” because the directions of their responses did not follow the rotation of the monkey but remained constant relative to the environment

span.label: the third group - THE LARGEST, AND UNNAMED: 12 of the 32 rotated neurons had their responses reversibly extinguished, against 11 egocentric and 9 allocentric, so the plurality of the sample falls outside the dichotomy that the key words carry
span.quote: Thirty-two of 106 neurons were also tested by rotating the monkey. The directionally differentiating responsiveness of 1 1 neurons followed the monkey (egocentric neurons), that of 9 remained in place in the environment (allocentric neurons), and responses of 12 were reversibly extinguished when the monkey was rotated

span.label: builds-on → O'Keefe and Conway, 1978 (rat hippocampus)
span.quote: This means that, consistent with a previous study of the rat hippocampus (O'Keefe and Conway, 1978), some neurons in the HF of the monkey may be involved in the representation of relations between stimuli through both vision and audition.

span.label: replicates → Creutzfeldt, 1990; Vidyasagar et al., 1991 (hippocampal neurons activated by human actions)
span.quote: This report is very similar to the present results in that selective neurons tended to respond to human action.

span.label: extends → Feigenbaum and Rolls (1991)
span.quote: Responsiveness of the neurons that was changed by movement of the apparatus may represent relations between the test stimulus and background stimuli fixed on the apparatus, and these might correspond to neurons with responses in the frame-of-reference of allocentric coordinates reported by Feigenbaum and Rolls (1991).

span.label: egocentric —contrasted-with→ allocentric
span.note: differs in: whether the response direction followed the rotated monkey or stayed fixed to the environment · strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Thirty-two of 106 neurons were also tested by rotating the monkey. The directionally differentiating responsiveness of 1 1 neurons followed the monkey (egocentric neurons), that of 9 remained in place in the environment (allocentric neurons), and responses of 12 were reversibly extinguished when the monkey was rotated

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: Responses to the presented stimuli were compared by one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with significance at Pc.05.

span.label: p-value
span.quote: Magnitudes of responses were almost the same for all kinds of different auditory stimuli presented from the left posterior direction (B) (ANOVA, P > . 1).

span.label: chi-squared
span.quote: These neurons were located throughout the rostrocaudal extent of the HF, but tended to be located caudally (chi-square test, fY.01).

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: Each histogram, mean and SEM of response size of five presentations of each stimulus.

span.label: Only about one in ten hippocampal-formation neurons recorded (106 of 1,047) responded preferentially to stimuli coming from one or more particular directions.
span.quote: Of 1,047 neurons recorded, 106 (10.1%) responded to some stimuli from one or more directions.

span.label: Of the 106 direction-sensitive neurons, 49 responded to vision only, 35 to audition only, and 22 to both modalities.
span.quote: Of these 106 neurons with directionally differentiating responsiveness, 49 responded to visual stimulation, 35 responded to auditory stimulation, and 22 responded to both visual and auditory stimulation.

span.label: Visually driven neurons preferred stimuli from the right anterior direction whereas auditory ones preferred stimuli from behind the monkey.
span.quote: The vision-responsive neurons tended to respond to stimulation presented from the right anterior direction, and the sound-responsiveness neurons tended to respond more to stimulation presented from the posterior.

span.label: Moving the experimental apparatus, which the monkey could see, altered the responses of 36 of the 59 neurons tested that way.
span.quote: Changing the location of the experimental apparatus modified the responses of 36 of 59 neurons.

span.label: For 24 of the affected neurons the preferred direction stayed the same but the response in that direction was strongly weakened or reversibly abolished.
span.quote: For the other 24, the preferred direction did not change, but responses in the preferred direction were very weakened, or the directionally differentiating responses were reversibly extinguished.

span.label: Rotating the monkey showed that 11 neurons carried their preferred direction with the animal, making them egocentric.
span.quote: When the monkey was rotated, the directionally differentiating responsiveness of 11 neurons followed the monkey.

span.label: Nine neurons kept their preferred direction anchored to the room rather than to the animal, making them allocentric.
span.quote: The directionally differentiating responsiveness of nine neurons remained in place in the environment and did not follow the monkey.

span.label: Twelve further neurons lost their directional selectivity altogether while the monkey was rotated, and regained it afterwards.
span.quote: The directionally differentiating responsiveness of 12 other neurons was reversibly extinguished when the monkey was rotated.

span.label: Response size depended on exactly where the visible apparatus stood, not merely on whether it was visible at all.
span.quote: The response magnitude also depended on the precise location of the apparatus when the monkey could see it.

span.label: Stimulus-selective auditory neurons responded to complex experimenter-produced sounds - footsteps, a chair moving, a door opening, a data recorder being switched, board tapping and paper crumpling - rather than to pure tones.
span.quote: All of these neurons exhibited strongly selective responses to complex sounds made by the experimenter: seven responded to a step, four to the sound of a chair moving, two to the sound of a door opening, two to a data recorder being switched, two to board tapping, one to the sound of paper crumpling.

span.label: Direction-sensitive neurons were found along the whole rostrocaudal axis of the hippocampal formation but were concentrated caudally.
span.quote: These neurons were located throughout the rostrocaudal extent of the HF, but tended to be located caudally (chi-square test, fY.01).

span.label: Eye position and eye movement did not account for the visual responses of most of these neurons.
span.quote: Judging from EOGs, television monitoring, and inspection of experimenter, there was no clear correlation between visual responses of most neurons and initial eye position or eye movement.

span.label: In the 22 bimodal neurons the visual and auditory preferred directions coincided in only half of the cells (11 of 22).
span.quote: Of the 22 visual plus auditory neurons with directionally differentiating responsiveness, the visual and auditory responses of 11 overlapped (4, left anterior; 2, anterior; 5, right anterior) and responses of 11 did not overlap direction.

span.label: The subicular complex held a higher share of neurons whose directional responsiveness changed when the apparatus moved (8 of 10) than the dentate gyrus, CA3 or CA1, which were split roughly evenly.
span.quote: In the subicular complex, the number of neurons that changed their directionally differentiating responsiveness when the location of the experimental apparatus was changed exceeded the number of stable neurons that did not change (8 of 10 changed, 2 of 10 stable), but there were no clear differences between the numbers of these neurons in other areas (dentate gyrus: 7 of 13 changed, 6 of 13 stable; CA3: 8 of 16 changed, 8 of 16 stable; CAI: 10 of 17 changed, 7 of 17 stable; EC: 2 of 2 changed; PH: 1 of 1 changed).

span.label: directionally differentiating responsiveness
span.quote: We use the term directionally differentiating since the neurons responded differently when stimuli were presented from different positions (or directions) around the monkey.

span.label: background stimuli
span.quote: Background stimuli is a general term meaning stimuli that could provide spatial reference for the test stimulus.

span.label: egocentric neurons
span.quote: We designate these neurons as “egocentric,” because the directions of their responses followed the rotation of the monkey, and these responses were considered to represent relations between the test stimulus and background stimuli on the monkey or on the restraining device that rotated with the monkey.

span.label: allocentric neurons
span.quote: We designated these neurons as “allocentric,” because the directions of their responses did not follow the rotation of the monkey but remained constant relative to the environment, and these responses were considered to represent relations between test stimulus and background stimuli fixed in the environment.

span.label: selective group of neurons
span.quote: In the other group, responsiveness depended on the nature of the stimulus, and these neurons tended to respond more to some stimuli than to others (selective group, n = 42).

span.label: direction of stimulus presentation relative to the monkey
span.term: direction of stimulus presentation relative to the monkey
span.quote: A few kinds of sounds were similarly presented five or more times each from the left anterior, anterior, right anterior, right posterior, posterior, and left posterior directions.

span.label: location of the experimental apparatus in the room
span.term: location of the experimental apparatus in the room
span.quote: The experimental apparatus in front of the monkey was moved to several places in the experimental room.

span.label: rotation of the monkey chair (45 degrees left / right)
span.term: rotation of the monkey chair (45 degrees left / right)
span.quote: The monkey chair was rotated 45” to the left and then 45” to the right of the experimental apparatus, and the test stimuli remained in their initial positions.

span.label: single-neuron firing during the first second after stimulus onset
span.term: single-neuron firing during the first second after stimulus onset
span.quote: Neuronal responses for the first 1.0 seconds after presentation were averaged for each of several stimulus presentations.

span.label: position of the monkey in the environment
span.term: position of the monkey in the environment
span.quote: Fifty-nine of 106 neurons were tested by changing the location of experimental apparatus in front of the monkey while the monkey’s position was fixed in the environment.

span.label: intensity of computer-synthesized sounds
span.quote: The intensity of computer-synthesized sounds was usually controlled to about 80 dB.

span.label: 106 (10.1%) — number and share of the 1,047 recorded neurons that showed direction-dependent responses
span.quote: Of 1,047 neurons recorded, 106 (10.1%) responded to some stimuli from one or more directions.

span.label: 36 of 59 — neurons whose responsiveness changed when the experimental apparatus was moved
span.quote: Changing the location of the experimental apparatus modified the responses of 36 of 59 neurons.

span.label: 11 — egocentric neurons whose preferred direction followed the rotated monkey
span.quote: When the monkey was rotated, the directionally differentiating responsiveness of 11 neurons followed the monkey.

span.label: nine — allocentric neurons whose preferred direction stayed fixed to the room
span.quote: The directionally differentiating responsiveness of nine neurons remained in place in the environment and did not follow the monkey.

span.label: 12 — neurons whose directional responsiveness disappeared reversibly during rotation
span.quote: The directionally differentiating responsiveness of 12 other neurons was reversibly extinguished when the monkey was rotated.

span.label: n = 42 — neurons classed as stimulus-selective among the 81 tested with more than ten stimuli
span.quote: In the other group, responsiveness depended on the nature of the stimulus, and these neurons tended to respond more to some stimuli than to others (selective group, n = 42).

span.label: about 80 dB — intensity at which computer-synthesized sounds were presented
span.quote: The intensity of computer-synthesized sounds was usually controlled to about 80 dB.
